incidents.vector: Voice-phishing (vishing) calls to employees yielded credentials used to take over Okta single sign-on accounts.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim theft of 284 million patient records; McKesson is managing fallout from an ongoing data-theft extortion attempt.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the C-Track court case management platform from March until discovery on June 30; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Sealed court records and personal data (SSNs, driver's licenses, medical and insurance data) exposed for courts in at least 12 US states, the US Virgin Islands, and Ontario, Canada.

incidents.victim: Latin American government, transport, water and financial organizations
incidents.vector: Two AI-assisted intrusion campaigns: living-off-the-land data theft against Mexican and Ecuadorian government and water entities, and job-themed phishing with custom remote-access trojans against Brazilian financial firms.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data exfiltrated from a Mexican transportation organization, federal ministries and municipal water utilities; attackers used self-hosted AI chat tools to generate attack scripts. Both campaigns remain active.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two zero-day flaws (CVE-2026-83548 SSRF, CVSS 10.0, and CVE-2026-83549 command injection) chained for unauthenticated remote code execution on SMA 1000 remote-access gateways.
incidents.impact: Confirmed in-the-wild compromises of internet-facing enterprise VPN gateways; SonicWall urges immediate patching, credential resets, and re-imaging of any appliance showing indicators of compromise.

incidents.vector: Breached a public API endpoint, then used autonomous AI agents to map the network, harvest secrets-management credentials, hijack CI/CD pipelines and steal cloud keys.
incidents.impact: Weeks of intrusion tradecraft compressed into under 10 hours using 50+ attack techniques; the victim's own cloud AI infrastructure was hijacked as attack infrastructure before a ransomware extortion demand.

incidents.vector: Attackers posing as IT helpdesk via external Microsoft Teams chats and calls talk users into granting remote-control sessions, then silently install a Node.js-based backdoor.
incidents.impact: Hands-on-keyboard intruders gain credential-backed access, capture screens, enumerate Active Directory, and pivot toward domain controllers — activity consistent with pre-ransomware staging.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of old, unpatched vulnerabilities in an internet-facing ownCloud file-sharing server for initial access.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole reactor databases, personnel records, and credential stores from the Philippines' nuclear agency.

incidents.victim: Serbian student activists, an MP and a local official
incidents.vector: Commercial spyware deployed via a zero-click iPhone exploit and via installs on phones seized during police questioning.
incidents.impact: 14 people targeted in the largest documented spyware wave in Serbia to date, ahead of March local and October parliamentary elections; researchers point to Serbian police or intelligence services.

incidents.vector: Exploited a bug in the underlying Cosmos blockchain platform; the same flaw was used against six other platforms the prior week.
incidents.impact: Attacker initially made off with $74 million in crypto tokens; $68 million was clawed back within hours. Cosmos halted all activity pending a fix.

incidents.vector: Exploiting poorly secured VPNs and remote-access tools, internet-facing application flaws, and credentials stolen from business partners to deploy custom ransomware.
incidents.impact: At least seven Russian organizations hit with multimillion-dollar ransom demands by a rebranded pro-Ukrainian group running custom ransomware, loaders and security-killing tools; stolen data may also feed follow-on operations.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into the company's Amazon Web Services infrastructure over roughly two weeks in December 2025.
incidents.impact: More than 9.5 million people's names, SSNs, medical, financial and insurance data stolen; at least 30 healthcare organizations that used Aesto's archiving services are affected.

incidents.victim: US government agencies, telecoms, hospitals, financial institutions (targeted)
incidents.vector: A private Chinese company operated a distributed vulnerability-scanning system and a covert relay network of compromised IoT devices to obfuscate Chinese espionage traffic.
incidents.impact: US DOJ seized domains and disrupted both systems, which supported nearly a decade of targeting including federal agencies and the US Senate; China is expected to rebuild, as prior botnet disruptions show.

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Breach of the ATF's lawful-intercept (CALEA) system; method of entry not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: 6.3 GB of claimed stolen data briefly published, including names, phone numbers and IP addresses of investigation targets and mobile-phone forensic data. ATF has confirmed it is investigating the breach.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft and identity fraud
incidents.vector: Apparent long-running, ongoing exfiltration from a major identity verification provider whose scanners are used by rental car firms, dispensaries, hotels and retailers.
incidents.impact: A new dark-web service is selling scans of 153M+ US and Canadian driver's licenses, including those of senior US officials, with ~400,000 new records added in 24 hours. FBI has opened an inquiry.

incidents.vector: 20-year-old polymorphic file-infecting malware forming a peer-to-peer botnet used to deliver payloads, primarily a clipboard hijacker that swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike, DOJ, FBI, Europol and partners sinkholed the botnet on Aug 31, permanently isolating infected machines from the operator; organizations should check for beaconing to the published sinkhole indicators.

incidents.vector: Server intrusion and data exfiltration in August, followed by an extortion threat to publish the stolen data.
incidents.impact: Patient, employee, provider and confidential financial data stolen from the operator of 27 hospitals in 12 states; a class action has been filed and the extortion attempt continues.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a critical authentication bypass (CVE-2026-82329, CVSS 9.8) within days of disclosure to mint admin tokens on internet-exposed repository servers.
incidents.impact: Attackers are gaining administrative control of software artifact repositories and enumerating users, credentials and federation topology — a direct path to software supply chain tampering. Added to CISA's KEV catalog.

incidents.vector: OAuth consent phishing over a commercial messaging app: victims are tricked into approving a malicious cloud application, bypassing passwords and MFA.
incidents.impact: FBI alert warns attackers gain persistent access to email and files of high-profile targets and their families; access survives password changes until the token is revoked.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a Stripe/WooCommerce payment integration used by two fundraising projects for online auctions in mid-August.
incidents.impact: Donor email addresses and partial card data exposed — dangerous data given Russian criminal penalties for donating to 'undesirable' organizations; Stripe blocked the access before full database theft.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to internal information systems at a subsidiary in mid-August; contained under the company's incident response plan.
incidents.impact: Internal patient ID numbers for 1,400+ US records, identifying data for fewer than 50 patients, and provider/employee contact details exposed; no device access or operational impact. Disclosed via SEC 8-K.

incidents.victim: China-based operations of multinationals; Chinese-speaking users
incidents.industry: Healthcare / manufacturing / gaming / logistics / government / education
incidents.vector: Counterfeit software-download sites impersonating trusted vendors (Razer, Microsoft Edge, Kaspersky and others) serve dynamically generated malicious installers.
incidents.impact: Compromises across multiple organizations and industries; malware establishes persistence, weakens security tooling and connects to attacker cloud infrastructure. Campaign remains active.

incidents.vector: 33-hour BGP hijack of the vendor's IP space with a forged, RPKI-valid route; attackers obtained a TLS certificate and served malicious updates from a cloned site.
incidents.impact: Hosting providers that pulled Virtualizor updates during the window may be compromised; payment data submitted during the hijack is likely stolen. Affected-user count is unknown because all traffic passed through attacker infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain and Türkiye
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures dropped a lightweight batch-script backdoor that abuses legitimate webhook services for command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Initial-access campaigns from late September 2025 through April 2026 targeting European defense and diplomatic entities, likely collecting intelligence around Moldova's elections and NATO-adjacent governance.
